metadata.note: Georgia Northern main line Boston (originally Pidcock) - Moultrie - Doerun - Ticknor - Albany, about 68 mi, built in stages 1893-1905, plus the Flint River and Northeastern (Pelham - Ticknor), a separate company. One feature per drawable span and operator: the Boston and Albany (of Georgia) ran the first trains 1893-1894 and is split from the Georgia Northern (legally distinct after a receivership sale); the 1905 relocation of the south end from Pidcock to Boston gives two southern pieces; the northward extensions of 1899 (Doerun), 1904 (Ticknor) and 1905 (Albany) each have their own geometry. The Boston and Albany Railroad (of Georgia) is not the Massachusetts Boston and Albany and carries its own colour.

metadata.ownership_split: Boston and Albany (of Georgia) 1893-1894 -> Georgia Northern from the 30 Jan 1895 card (ICC: property passed 7 Feb 1895). Not splits: Pidcock acquisitions of the FR&NE (1910), GAS&C (1922) and A&N (1939), each run under its own name; Southern control 1966 came after passenger service.

properties.geometry_source: Straight line Pidcock - Oak Lawn (no surviving alignment); OpenStreetMap (ODbL) way 124281259, abandoned grade tagged old_railway_operator=Georgia Northern, Oak Lawn - Moultrie; Moultrie-Schley Junction Line ways into Moultrie.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 28.31 mi against documented about 30.0 (Fowler: Pidcock 0 - Oak Lawn 7, Oak Lawn 5.8 - Moultrie 28.8 from Boston) and 31 operated (1894 Official Railway List, via railga). Approximated: Pidcock - Oak Lawn, one straight line of 4.95 mi against Fowler's 7 mi; the original 1893-1905 southern end was relocated to Boston in 1905 and no trace of it was found in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap, so the straight chord understates the route by about 2 mi. Pidcock is placed on today's CSX Thomasville Subdivision (the SF&W junction) 31 m from the Pidcock hamlet node; Oak Lawn is the Oaklawn hamlet node (OSM 153966407) projected onto the grade, 263 m away, at 5.66 mi from Boston against Fowler's 5.8. Oak Lawn - Moultrie (23.36 mi against Fowler's 23.0) is traced on the OSM abandoned Georgia Northern grade through Barwick (11 m), Pavo (0.3 km) and Autreyville (0.3 km); that grade is the road's final alignment, taken to be the 1893 one because no relocation north of Oak Lawn is recorded. The last ~1.3 mi into Moultrie follows tracks now tagged Moultrie-Schley Junction Line (Georgia and Florida Railway); the Moultrie end point is approximate (the 1893 depot site was not located).

segments.note: First scheduled train into Moultrie 21 Mar 1893 (Savannah Morning News 13 Feb 1900, retrospective; corroborated by a 1927 Wiregrass Farmer obituary and Southern's 1968 75th-anniversary event). Contemporary 1893-94 papers name the operating company the Boston and Albany Railroad, C. W. Pidcock superintendent; in receivership from June 1893 (Tifton Gazette 16 Jun 1893). Headway from the only schedule seen for this operator: 'Train No. 5, on the Boston and Albany railroad, now leaves Pidcock for Moultrie at 3:15 p.m. daily and train No. 6 leaves Moultrie at 7 a.m.' (Thomasville Daily Times-Enterprise 7 Aug 1894) - one round trip a day; 1893 frequency is assumed the same. Ends 1894: trains ran as the Georgia Northern from the timetable effective 30 Jan 1895 (property passed 7 Feb 1895 per the ICC). Source conflict: railga says the B&A built no track and the Pidcocks ran the line as the Georgia Northern without a charter; the ICC and contemporary papers say the B&A operated it. A different railroad from the Massachusetts Boston and Albany, so it carries its own company string and colour.
sources: Segment-level: Savannah Morning News 13 Feb 1900 p9 (first train 21 Mar 1893); Thomasville Daily Times-Enterprise 7 Apr 1893 p1 and 7 Aug 1894 p1; Tifton Gazette 16 Jun 1893 p1, via Georgia Historic Newspapers, as read by the research report

properties.geometry_quality: Approximated in full: one straight line Pidcock - Oak Lawn of 4.95 mi against Fowler's 7 mi (Pidcock 0, Lake Station 2, Oak Lawn 7), so it understates the route by about 2 mi and does not pass through Lake Station, Spangler or Phoebe, whose sites were not located. railga describes the 1905 relocation as 'the southernmost four miles', which does not square exactly with Fowler's 7 mi Pidcock - Oak Lawn against 5.8 mi Boston - Oak Lawn; not reconciled. This is the pre-1905 alignment, deliberately not drawn on the Boston line (Rule 2).

Pidcock, Supt.), trains Nos. 5/6 passenger Pidcock - Moultrie, printed through 1895; further cards 1895, 1896, 5 Apr 1897 (printed 19 Oct 1897) list Pidcock - Lake Station - ... - Moultrie. Ends 1905: 'the Georgia Northern railroad ran its trains into Boston the 4th of October, 1905' (Weekly Times-Enterprise 16 Mar 1906). Whether any passenger train still used Pidcock after that is not established and none is drawn. Headway: one round trip a day per the 1895 cards; later years in the span are an estimate carried forward.

segments.note: Opened to passengers 4 Oct 1905, when 'the Georgia Northern railroad ran its trains into Boston' (Weekly Times-Enterprise 16 Mar 1906); the 'Albany - Boston Line' card effective the same day (Albany Daily Herald 12 Feb 1906). Connection at Boston with the ACL. [OPEN] 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: the Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules of Sept 1951) prints a Georgia Northern rail table naming Boston (footnote 'With A.C.L.') and train No. 11, but its OCR does not tie the surviving times to stations, so which trains ran south of Moultrie is not shown. The 30 Oct 1953 discontinuance notice covers only Albany - Moultrie and is silent on Moultrie - Boston. Service here may have ended before 1951 or after 1953; no source dates it. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate: the 1905 card's southern working is not fully read, and the 'twice daily, except Sunday, local Boston to Moultrie' of an undated rrpicturearchives caption and Hensley's 'six passenger trains a day' in the 1930s are secondary. Boston - Barwick was abandoned in 1971 (railga) - a freight-era date, not a passenger end.
sources: Segment-level: Weekly Times-Enterprise and South Georgia Progress 16 Mar 1906 p12; Albany Daily Herald 12 Feb 1906 p2 (card eff. 4 Oct 1905), via Georgia Historic Newspapers; Feb 1952 Official Guide GN table (Sept 1951 schedules, partial OCR), as read by the research report

segments.note: Georgia Northern from the card 'to take effect on and after Jan. 30th, 1895' (trains Nos. 5/6, passenger, Pidcock - Moultrie); further cards Aug and Dec 1895, Apr 1897, Jan 1899. In May 1895 'a new coach and engine has been put on the road' (Savannah Morning News 30 May 1895). 1893-1894 on this track is drawn under the Boston and Albany. Headway: one round trip a day per the 1895 cards; the 1899 card notes a coach carried on another train too (OCR fragment), so later years in this span are an estimate. Segment ends Oct 1905 when the southern terminus moved to Boston and through Albany - Boston trains began.

segments.note: Through 'Albany - Boston Line' from the card effective 4 Oct 1905 (Albany Daily Herald 12 Feb 1906). A Georgia Northern 'motor train' with motorman and porter was at Moultrie in Aug 1946 (Omega News 1 Aug 1946; which side of Moultrie not stated); gas motor cars were bought from 1932 especially for the rural south end (Hensley, taplines.net, secondary). [OPEN] 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: the Feb 1952 Official Guide (schedules of Sept 1951) prints a Georgia Northern rail table naming Boston (footnote 'With A.C.L.') and train No. 11, but its OCR does not tie the surviving times to stations, so which trains ran south of Moultrie is not shown. The 30 Oct 1953 discontinuance notice covers only Albany - Moultrie and is silent on Moultrie - Boston. Service here may have ended before 1951 or after 1953; no source dates it. Do not extend without evidence. Headway is an estimate (secondary sources: six trains a day in the 1930s; a twice-daily-except-Sunday Boston - Moultrie motor-car local, undated). Pavo - Moultrie was abandoned in 1990 - a freight-era date.
sources: Segment-level: Albany Daily Herald 12 Feb 1906 p2 (card eff. 4 Oct 1905); Omega News 1 Aug 1946 p1, via Georgia Historic Newspapers; Feb 1952 Official Guide GN table (Sept 1951 schedules, partial OCR), as read by the research report

segments.note: Track was 'completed nine miles above Moultrie' with Doerun to be 'for the time ... the northern terminus' (Macon Telegraph 25 Aug 1898); first card seen naming Doerun is the GN 'Local Time Table, Effective Jan. 30th, 1899' (Moultrie ... Schley, Sigsbee, Dewey, Dewey Junction, Arrive Doerun; Thomasville Daily Times-Enterprise 8 Apr 1899). Service between Aug 1898 and Jan 1899 is unproven, so 1899 is the start. June 1900 card lists Doerun, Moultrie, Pidcock. Headway is an estimate (one round trip, as on the south end).

segments.note: Through Albany - Moultrie trains from the card effective 4 Oct 1905: No. 2 daily Albany 7:30 am - Doerun 8:30 - Moultrie 9:10, No. 4 Sunday only, No. 6 daily except Sunday, northbound Nos. 1/3 (Albany Daily Herald 12 Feb 1906). [OPEN] 1953 is the year of the APPLICATION to discontinue, not a known last-train date: a 'Notice to the Public' dated 30 Oct 1953, signed by the Georgia Northern Railway Company, says it has applied to the Georgia Public Service Commission to discontinue all passenger trains between Albany and Moultrie, Nos. 1-6, hearing 12 Nov 1953, so three round trips a day were still running in late Oct 1953. The Commission's order and the last train were not found; service may have run into 1954. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end. Do not extend without evidence, and do not use the c.1970 date of the photograph of the notice. Headway: three round trips (Nos. 1-6) in 1953 per the notice; 1905 had two daily pairs plus a Sunday train; years between are an estimate.

properties.line: Flint River and Northeastern: Pelham – Ticknor
properties.speed_source: estimated: no running times were read from the 1904 or 1921 cards; a round figure for a light logging-line conversion
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) way 164908382, abandoned grade named Flint River and Northeastern Railroad (old_railway_operator=Georgia Northern).
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 23.29 mi against documented 24 (Fowler; railga '24 miles'; the 1904 card gives 25 to Doerun, which includes 1.5 mi of Georgia Northern track not drawn here), all on the one OSM abandoned FR&NE way through Hinsonton (0.1 km) and Sale City (0 km). No straight-line leg. The Pelham end is the south end of that way at the ACL; Ticknor is the junction node with the Georgia Northern.

segments.note: Converted from a logging line in 1904 (railga); timetable in the Camilla Enterprise 12 Feb 1904 (Pelham - Wilma - Maples - Hinson - Floride - Akridge - Sale City - Tuton - Tichnor - Doerun). Last newspaper card: 'Schedule effective April 17, 1921', Nos. 8/9 daily except Sunday Pelham - Sale City - Ticknor, 'All trains connect at Ticknor with Georgia Northern trains' (Pelham Journal, printed through 6 Jan 1922). [OPEN] end: 1926 rests on Fowler's listing of a 1926 Official Guide ('Cotton (2nd)? 1926G'), not on a timetable seen; it is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - service may have run on toward the 1946 abandonment, which is a freight-era date, not a passenger end. Do not extend without evidence. Run under its own name throughout: the Pidcocks/GN bought it in 1910 but it kept its separate identity and timetable, so it is not split to the GN. Headway: one round trip daily except Sunday in 1921; other years an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: Camilla Enterprise 12 Feb 1904 p1; Pelham Journal 10 Sep 1920, 2 Sep 1921, 4 Nov 1921, 2 Dec 1921, via Georgia Historic Newspapers; Fowler's Georgia station list section 96 (1926G listing), as read by the research report
